memory_update.text: SPSC should be the primary Layer 1B underfollowed candidate for the retail_supplier_networks node because it most directly maps to retailer-supplier EDI, compliance logic, trading-partner maps, and recurring-revenue network durability.

OTEX belongs in the discovery lane as a hidden B2B/EDI network asset inside a broader enterprise software company; later layers must isolate Business Network segment durability and retail/CPG exposure.
DSGX is an adjacent network candidate: strongest around logistics/trade-compliance data rails, with retail-supplier connectivity relevance that requires segment and customer-materiality verification.

MANH is useful as a reference/adjacent leader for retail order-management and fulfillment orchestration, but it should not be treated as the pure retailer-supplier EDI chokepoint without additional evidence.

Need a later search pass for smaller public or newly public EDI/API specialists, retail compliance software, product-content syndication, chargeback/deduction management, GS1/data-quality vendors, and retailer onboarding/certification bottlenecks; many likely remain private.

node: Retailer-supplier connectivity networks, EDI/API rails, compliance maps, and trading-partner data
summary: Expanded the public-market universe around retailer-supplier connectivity networks with a two-lane funnel. SPS Commerce is the closest pure-play underfollowed node match: retailer/supplier EDI, compliance logic, recurring revenue, and a large trading-partner network. OpenText and Descartes are less pure but potentially underappreciated because the relevant B2B/EDI rails are embedded inside broader enterprise information-management or logistics-network businesses. Manhattan Associates is included as a reference/adjacent leader because retail order-management and fulfillment orchestration sit next to the same operational chokepoint, though its exposure is more omnichannel execution than retailer-supplier EDI maps.
